hero.headline: Riviera Beach named only Florida city to receive 2026 All-America City Award
hero.teaser: Riviera Beach was named one of just 10 communities in the U.S. to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League, and it was the only Florida city selected for the honor this year.
hero.body:
Riviera Beach has earned one of the nation's most prestigious civic honors, becoming the only Florida community selected for the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League. The city was one of just 10 U.S. communities to receive this distinction. The award recognizes municipalities that bring together residents, local government, businesses and organizations to address community challenges and create meaningful, lasting change. City leaders announced the achievement during the National Civic League conference in Denver, where Riviera Beach presented its efforts to strengthen community engagement and civic participation.

Mayor Douglas Lawson expressed pride in the recognition, stating that "Little old Riviera Beach is one of the biggest, brightest, shining stars." He credited years of work to revitalize the city and improve the quality of life for residents. Lawson said the community is witnessing the changes and reimagining efforts the city set out to accomplish long ago. City leaders emphasized that the award reflects their commitment to improving civic health, building trust between residents and local government, and enabling residents to shape the city's future directly.

The city highlighted several key programs in its award application that demonstrate its investment in civic participation. The Riviera Beach Youth Council engages high school students in civic leadership and advocacy. The Citizens Leadership Academy provides civic education with a 98 percent completion rate. The Neighborhood Reclaim Home Rehabilitation Program awards mini-grants to longtime homeowners for necessary repairs. Councilwoman KaShamba Miller-Anderson noted the city is implementing innovative approaches to ensure residents actively participate in community development. She stated that the award "brings back community pride" and reinforces positive momentum throughout Riviera Beach.

The All-America City Award, presented annually since 1949, stands as one of the nation's most respected honors for community achievement. City officials believe the designation positions Riviera Beach for future opportunities and continued growth while signaling to the nation that collaboration and resident involvement drive results. The nine other communities receiving the award are Chelsea, Massachusetts; Franklin, Tennessee; Harlingen, Texas; Montgomery, Alabama; Morrisville, North Carolina; Norfolk, Virginia; North Charleston, South Carolina; Roanoke, Virginia; and Woodburn, Oregon.

cards.headline: Martin County School Board fights judge's order to reinstate teacher suspended over Charlie Kirk comments
cards.teaser: The Martin County School Board filed a court challenge Thursday against a judge's recommendation to reinstate a Spectrum Academy teacher who was suspended last .
cards.body:
The Martin County School Board is pushing back against a judge's recommendation to reinstate Matt Theobald, a social studies teacher at Spectrum Academy since 2009, who was suspended last year following controversial social media comments about Charlie Kirk. In a Thursday court filing, the school board argued that Administrative Law Judge Jodi-Ann Vanessa Livingstone erred in her recommendation, saying "numerous findings ... are not based upon competent substantial evidence." The board's attorney claims Theobald's Facebook post about Kirk, in which he labeled the conservative activist as racist, misogynistic and a neo-Nazi, was a "serious offense" and that removing him was appropriate.

In her order issued last month, Livingstone cited a recent Florida Fifth District Court of Appeal ruling that said disciplining a teacher for personal Facebook posts made off school grounds, on personal equipment, with no student involvement, violated the teacher's First Amendment rights. The judge also recommended Theobald be awarded back pay and benefits. According to an investigation report obtained by WPTV, Theobald admitted writing the comments but said they were posted on his mother's private Facebook page "within a discussion among personal acquaintances" and were not intended for public view.

cards.headline: Secretary of State Byrd Moves to Block Paula Stark from Ballot After Incomplete Filing
cards.body:
Secretary of State Cord Byrd is asking courts to keep St. Cloud Republican Paula Stark off the ballot after she failed to submit required paperwork before the June 12 qualifying deadline. Stark submitted her materials just 30 minutes before the noon deadline, but state employees say she never filed Form 6, a public disclosure of financial interests. Stark has since sued to get on the ballot, claiming her treasurer Joel Davis accidentally received the form back during the submission process.

In response to her lawsuit, Byrd cast doubt on Stark's account of events. Five state employees submitted sworn declarations stating that Davis never submitted Form 6 and was not accidentally handed it back when he turned in other paperwork. Election Records Division Bureau Chief Erica Ikay Reeve noted in court filings that Stark still has not submitted Form 6 three weeks after the qualifying deadline. "Without seeing the Form 6 that was allegedly submitted, we cannot review it for facial sufficiency in order to determine if Candidate Stark would have qualified," Reeve stated. Byrd argued that Stark and Davis should have exercised greater care by questioning why the form was allegedly returned or by submitting documents earlier rather than waiting until the final moments before the deadline.

Reeve documented a troubling pattern of paperwork violations in Stark's campaign history. Davis has filed campaign finance reports more than a month late, reported excessive contributions, and maintained an incorrect address on file. Audits in the 2022 and 2024 election cycles found inconsistent amounts transferred between accounts and accounting discrepancies. The state revoked Stark's Friends of Paula political committee in November over 16,000 dollars in unpaid fines from missed campaign finance deadlines. In the 2024 cycle, a failure to pay a late report fine upheld by the Florida Elections Commission was referred to debt collection in November 2025. Of the 12 candidates who failed to properly submit Form 6, half of them corrected the problems and still qualified.

Byrd emphasized the time constraints in his court response, noting that ballots must be mailed to overseas military and their families by July 4, with vote-by-mail ballots due July 9 through 16. If Stark remains off the ballot, the August primary for House District 47 in Osceola and Orange counties becomes open to all voters choosing between Democrats Jorge Figueroa and Anthony Nieves. No other Republicans filed to run in the traditionally Democratic district, making Stark's exclusion a significant win for Florida Democrats.

cards.headline: Martin County maritime teams deploy two boats with medics for Fourth of July weekend
cards.teaser: Martin County Maritime Response Unit has two boats with medics on standby in the north and south as hundreds of boaters take to the water for the holiday weekend.
cards.body:
Lt. Brett Harry with Martin County Maritime Response Unit said the team is expecting hundreds of boaters on the water celebrating the Fourth of July weekend. The unit has deployed two boats with medics on standby in Martin County in the north and south to assist anyone in need.

Harry said the team is out on the water to help with anything from something as simple as a stubbed toe to cardiac issues, potential spinal injuries or other emergencies. Boaters like Brendan and Ashley Shannon launched from the ramps at Sandsprit Park in Martin County on Friday with their young daughter and puppy. The Shannons said safety is top of mind when hitting the water. Harry encouraged boaters to do their part by keeping their eyes on the water, having a designated driver, and packing life vests, whistles and flotation devices. "Just have fun and be safe," Harry said.

cards.headline: St. Petersburg Selects $8.1 Billion Plan to Redevelop Tropicana Field Site
cards.teaser: Mayor Ken Welch selected a proposal to transform 58 acres around Tropicana Field into a mixed-use district centered on a 13-acre civic park and permanent home for The Woodson African American Museum of Florida.
cards.body:
St. Petersburg selected The Burg Bid, an $8.1 billion proposal led by Blake Investment Partners and Related Group, to redevelop Tropicana Field and the surrounding Historic Gas Plant District. The plan calls for purchasing 58 acres of city-owned land for $275 million, with a $20 million deposit due when a purchase and sale agreement is executed. The team values the full land package at $405 million when factoring in $130 million in land the city would retain. The proposal centers on Samuel Davis Park, a 13-acre civic and cultural space that would anchor 18.5 acres of total public park space. The park would house The Woodson African American Museum of Florida, a planned Museum of Public Art, a Discovery Center, event lawns, a playground, a splash pad, cafe areas, public art and a concert lawn.

The Burg Bid calls for 3,600 income-restricted housing units over a 15-year buildout, with 1,800 units planned within the Historic Gas Plant District and another 1,800 on complementary sites elsewhere in St. Petersburg. The plan includes homeownership opportunities at a discount to market value. Development would occur in three phases of approximately five years each, with early work potentially beginning outside the Tropicana Field footprint before stadium demolition. The proposal also includes a surf wave attraction, recreation deck, multimodal hub, workforce and small-business center called the Collaboratorium, and Resilience Event Center. The Rays lease with the city ends after the 2028 season.

cards.headline: DeSantis Allies Accuse Lieutenant Governor's Wife of Running Anonymous Attack Accounts
cards.teaser: Multiple social media accounts critical of Governor Ron DeSantis were suddenly deactivated after prominent communications veterans tied them to Layla Collins, wife of Lieutenant Governor Jay Collins.
cards.body:
Christina Pushaw, a communications specialist in the Governor's Office, and Jeremy Redfern, Deputy Chief of Staff to Attorney General James Uthmeier, accused Layla Collins of operating anonymous social media accounts attacking Governor Ron DeSantis. Pushaw shared information from Promota CEO Robert Salvador showing that the account @FSUdude01670 appeared connected to a phone number similar to one known to be associated with Layla Collins. Florida Politics obtained screenshots verifying the connection through two-factor authentication, which displayed an attempt to access the account that triggered a message to an email address with letters starred out and a phone number showing only the last digits. Pushaw also identified a second account, @bobnamy1, that appeared tied to Layla Collins. She noted the account content consisted entirely of two types of posts: promoting Jay Collins and attacking people who did not endorse him, including the governor. Redfern stated that the FSUDude account was tied directly to her personal cell phone number.

Both accounts were deactivated after Pushaw and Redfern publicly leveled their criticisms. Both previously served as Press Secretaries for DeSantis. Redfern now works for Uthmeier, who has endorsed U.S. Representative Byron Donalds for Governor. DeSantis appointed Jay Collins as Lieutenant Governor last year but has declined to endorse a preferred successor in the Governor's race. DeSantis cannot seek a third term because of term limits. Florida Politics requested comments from Jay and Layla Collins.

cards.headline: Martin County Maritime Response Unit deploys medics as Fourth of July weekend brings hundreds of boaters
cards.teaser: Martin County Maritime Response Unit is deploying two boats with medics on standby this Fourth of July weekend as hundreds of boaters are expected on local wate.
cards.body:
Hundreds of boaters are expected on Florida waterways this Fourth of July weekend, prompting Martin County Maritime Response Unit to deploy additional resources. Lt. Brett Harry said his team will have two boats with medics on standby positioned in the north and south areas of Martin County to respond to emergencies ranging from minor injuries to cardiac events and potential spinal injuries.

Boaters launched Friday from Sandsprit Park in Martin County, including Brendan and Ashley Shannon, who arrived with their young daughter and puppy. The Shannons said safety is their top priority on the water. Lt. Harry urged boaters to keep their eyes on the water, designate a sober driver, and pack life vests, whistles and flotation devices. "Just have fun and be safe," Harry said.

hero.headline: Juno Beach residents demand fence replacement at JB-7 beach access as town considers costly fix
hero.teaser: Residents at the Colony Condos say people using the JB-7 public walkway are cutting through their private property since the town removed a fence in 2023 for safety reasons.
hero.body:
Residents at the Colony Condos in Juno Beach are facing an ongoing problem with trespassers since the town removed a protective fence in 2023 for safety reasons. The old barrier once clearly marked the boundary between the public JB-7 walkway and private property, but now only bushes separate the two areas. Without the fence, residents say beachgoers regularly cut through their land, parking in private spots and pushing through vegetation with coolers, fishing rods, and lawn chairs. Lori Hill, a Colony resident, explained that the issue becomes especially severe during summer months when visitors arrive unexpectedly and occupy private parking spaces for extended periods.

The situation has created tension between residents and beach visitors. Hill said that residents once confronted trespassers directly to explain the property was private, but these interactions frequently turned hostile. Colony residents now call police to handle the problem instead. Not all beachgoers acknowledge the conflict, however. Michael House, who regularly walks to JB-7 from a nearby public parking lot, said he has never witnessed the trespassing issues residents describe and noted that ample free parking exists in the area. He suggested that property damage or littering would be more significant concerns than boundary violations.

The fence dispute recently came before the Juno Beach Town Council, where officials clarified that the town holds no legal obligation to install a fence on the property. However, Vice Mayor Pro Tem DD Halpern expressed openness to exploring more affordable solutions. He suggested the town might consider helping residents with a lower-cost fence option or a combination of split rail fencing and shrubs to mark the boundary more clearly while reducing expenses.

The council has scheduled the fence question for discussion during its budget talks on July 15. Hill said residents remain hopeful that town officials will reinstall a barrier so that Colony Condos can reclaim their landscaping and private parking areas. The cost of replacing the fence could amount to six figures, making the budget decision a significant financial consideration for the town. Residents are waiting to see whether the council will prioritize the boundary solution or pursue alternative approaches during the upcoming budget meeting.

cards.headline: Boca Raton Community High School band to march in National Independence Day Parade
cards.teaser: The Boca Raton Community High School band will march a full mile along the National Mall on July 4, representing the entire state of Florida in Washington D.C.'s National Independence Day Parade.
cards.body:
The Boca Raton Community High School band has earned a coveted spot in Washington, D.C.'s National Independence Day Parade, representing the entire state of Florida. On July 4 at 10:30 a.m., the students will march a full mile along the National Mall, from Constitution Avenue to Independence Avenue. Only bands nominated by state officials receive invitations to this prestigious event.

Band Director Jenn Girdlestone expressed confidence in her students, saying she has full faith they will put their best foot forward and represent the country well. Junior Lola Cabezas acknowledged the pressure of performing for millions, if not billions, of viewers but expressed belief that the band will rise to the occasion. Senior Stephin Restivo said the team is laser-focused on nailing every detail, particularly the marching and timing of everything, so everyone can see what the Boca High band is capable of. The parade will be streamed live on YouTube for those who want to cheer on the band from home.

cards.headline: Breast cancer patient denied coverage for reconstruction surgery hours before procedure
cards.teaser: Beth Clark's insurance company, Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield, denied coverage for a reconstruction procedure involving GalaFlex mesh less than 24 hours before it was scheduled.
cards.body:
Beth Clark, 48, was diagnosed with invasive ductal carcinoma three months ago and planned a full double bilateral mastectomy with reconstruction. Less than 24 hours before her reconstruction surgery, her insurance company, Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield, denied coverage for the procedure. According to her denial letter, the surgery involving a surgical mesh called GalaFlex is still considered investigational with no or not enough proof it improves health. GalaFlex is a synthetic surgical mesh approved by the FDA for some uses in the body but not for breast reconstruction. In a 2023 letter to health care providers, the FDA stated that efficacy and safety for breast cancer patients have not been determined.

Despite the denial, Clark underwent reconstruction surgery with the GalaFlex mesh a little more than a week ago. Her plastic surgeon, Dr. Alicia Billington, who uses GalaFlex on most of her breast reconstruction patients, worked to make the procedure possible. Billington says the product gives patients the least amount of complications compared to other options. A spokesperson for Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield said the company regularly reviews coverage policies to ensure they are based on medical evidence and aligned with the latest treatment standards, adding that without FDA approval, the mesh does not currently meet the standards required for coverage. Clark and Billington are continuing to fight the denial.

cards.headline: Palm Beach County schools earn third consecutive A rating from state
cards.teaser: The School District of Palm Beach County received an A rating from the state for the third year in a row, with 143 district-operated schools rated A or B.
cards.body:
The School District of Palm Beach County received an "A" rating from the Florida Department of Education for the third consecutive year, reflecting strong student performance across all grade levels. This year, 143 district-operated schools, or 84%, were rated "A" or "B," up from 120 schools the previous year. The district achieved a record-setting 93.5% graduation rate. District leaders noted that 86% of seniors participated in college-level coursework through Advanced Placement, International Baccalaureate, Cambridge Advanced International Certificate of Education, or Dual Enrollment courses. Additionally, 144 recent graduates earned an associate degree alongside their high school diploma.

S.D. Spady Elementary School in Delray Beach made a dramatic leap from a "C" rating to an "A" this year under Principal Rona Tata, who has served as principal for 15 years. Three years ago, staff modified the school's early childhood curriculum program, which starts at age 3. Many of those students are now in third grade and performing at higher levels, contributing to the improved rating. Spady Elementary was one of four district schools to improve from a "C" to an "A" this year, alongside Dwight D. Eisenhower K-8, Glade View Elementary, and West Gate Elementary. Superintendent Mike Burke said the rating reflects the district's commitment to academic success.

cards.headline: Fourth of July cookout costs rise 4% this year as inflation hits holiday staples
cards.teaser: A Fourth of July meal for 10 now costs $73.82, up 4% from a year ago, according to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey.
cards.body:
A Fourth of July meal for 10 now costs $73.82, up 4% from a year ago, according to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey. Inflation is driving the price increases across cookout staples. Ground beef prices have risen 5.5%, while buns are up 7.7%. Strawberries have seen the steepest increase at 12.4% following a Florida frost, and ice cream prices have climbed 5.3%.

Not all cookout items have become more expensive. Potato prices are down this year, offering savings for those planning potato chips and salads. Corn prices have fluctuated, though locally grown corn from the Glades can provide the best value. Budgeting expert Andrea Woroch recommends shopping strategically by comparing prices across stores to find the best deals for items on your grocery list. She emphasized that reducing food waste is crucial for families, and said a meal plan is the best way to start.

hero.headline: Hobe Sound woman dies in home fire, community raises funds for fiance
hero.teaser: Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside the couple's home in Hobe Sound. Friends have launched a fundraiser to help her fiance Mark rebuild.
hero.body:
Misty Dawn White, 46, died in a house fire that broke out in her Hobe Sound home on Monday. She was discovered inside after emergency responders arrived at the scene. The sheriff's office has identified a possible electrical issue as the cause, though investigators continue to examine what happened. The fire destroyed much of the home and the possessions belonging to White and her fiancé Mark.

Word of White's death reached her close friend Nina Fenn through a phone call from Mark. Fenn, who had known White for eight years, has since become a key voice in sharing details about the tragedy and supporting those affected. "It's just a terrible shame and awful loss of life," Fenn said. Following the fire, friends and community members organized a fundraiser to help Mark rebuild his life after losing his home and belongings in the flames. Fenn described the situation as "completely a state of devastation" and has been working to support Mark however she can.

Fenn remembered White as a devoted Christian who had a passion for gardening and plants and played the piano. She noted that White was generous with others and always willing to help. "She was always the first to lend a hand," Fenn said. "She loves kids; she loves her kids. She loves people." Those who knew her say her kindness and generous spirit made a lasting impression on everyone around her. Fenn emphasized that White's memory will endure among those who loved her. "She's always been a good soul to me. She'll always be in our hearts," Fenn said.

The tragedy compounds an existing grief that Mark has already experienced. Fenn explained that Mark previously lost his only child, Jacob, in a tragic circumstance. The timing of White's death adds additional sorrow for those close to her. White's birthday fell on the Fourth of July, meaning she passed away just days before what would have been her birthday celebration. For Mark and White's loved ones, this convergence of loss underscores the depth of heartbreak the community is processing together.

cards.headline: Stuart downtown dock closing Sunday for $3 million renovation
cards.teaser: Stuart's downtown public dock will close July 6 for a year-long renovation that will nearly double capacity from 18 to 44 slips.
cards.body:
Stuart's downtown public dock will close July 6 for a $3 million renovation project expected to be completed by next Fourth of July. The project will nearly double the dock's capacity, expanding from 18 to 44 slips for both motorized and non-motorized vessels. Funding comes from a state grant and transportation impact fees. The renovation will include a 7,500 square foot fixed dock, a 1,400 square foot floating dock and a smaller floating platform.

Stuart Mayor Sean Reed said the upgrades serve multiple purposes beyond increasing capacity. "They're doing it to prevent storm damage during hurricanes and major storms," Reed said. "So the year of waiting will be worth it." With more than 1,400 boaters using the dock annually, the city is working to accommodate businesses and boaters who rely on it during the closure. Austin Kuyrkendall, director of operations for Tiki Taxi & Cruises, said the city is allowing the company to build a gate at the end of the downtown Stuart dock to board people at the non-floating section during construction.

cards.headline: Autonomous elevated transit proposed to connect West Palm Beach to airport
cards.teaser: California-based Glydways is proposing an elevated network of self-driving vehicles that would connect downtown West Palm Beach to President Donald J. Trump International Airport.
cards.body:
California-based autonomous transit company Glydways is proposing an elevated network of self-driving vehicles to connect downtown West Palm Beach to President Donald J. Trump International Airport, along with nearby Brightline and Tri-Rail stations. The company will present the proposal to Palm Beach County commissioners Tuesday for initial consideration. Glydways describes the system as a modern alternative to traditional transit such as light rail, streetcars and people movers, functioning like a "horizontal elevator" that carries passengers directly between destinations without traffic delays or intermediate stops.

Small autonomous electric vehicles carrying four to six passengers would travel along a dedicated elevated guideway built above existing roads. Glydways estimates travel times of seven minutes or less between the convention center and airport and roughly one to two minutes between Tri-Rail and the convention center. Senior Vice President Brian Gettinger said the system would cost "a small fraction" of a traditional light rail system while offering comparable passenger capacity, referencing previous South Florida light rail estimates of $400 million to $500 million per mile. Potential funding sources include Palm Beach County, the City of West Palm Beach, the Florida Department of Transportation, federal transit grants and public-private partnerships. Gettinger emphasized the service would be priced at transit levels, not private rideshare rates, and would require local employees for operations centers and maintenance facilities.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie advances land transfer for new Florida Turnpike interchange at Midway Road
cards.teaser: The Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation to assist with the interchange.
cards.body:
The Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance last month to transfer 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation for a partial interchange on Florida's Turnpike at Midway Road. Scott Samples, strategic communications manager for Port St. Lucie, said there is a significant gap between current Turnpike entrances and exits in the city. Samples explained the interchange addresses accessibility and accommodates growth expected over the next 20 to 50 years.

FDOT is constructing the $95 million Midway Road Widening Project to reduce congestion and improve safety. The first phase widens the road from two to four lanes between Selvitz Road and Jenkins Road, currently under construction. The second phase, from Jenkins Road to Glades Cut Off Road, remains in design with construction anticipated to begin in Summer 2027. FDOT is also improving the Turnpike bridge and designing the partial interchange. The project will include bike and pedestrian paths along with sidewalks. City council will vote on final approval for the land transfer at an upcoming meeting.

cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation to assist with a partial interchange on Florida's Turnpike.
cards.body:

FDOT has been constructing the $95 million Midway Road Widening Project to address congestion and safety. Crews are currently working on the first phase, widening the road from two lanes to four lanes from Selvitz Road to Jenkins Road. According to the FDOT website, the second widening phase from Jenkins Road to Glades Cut Off Road remains in the design phase, with construction anticipated to begin in Summer 2027. The partial Turnpike interchange is also still in the design phase. The project will add bike and pedestrian paths along with sidewalks. City council will vote on final approval to give the land at an upcoming meeting.

cards.headline: Stuart's downtown dock to close Monday for $3 million renovation, nearly doubling capacity
cards.teaser: Stuart's downtown public dock will close July 6 for a $3 million renovation projected to be complete by next Fourth of July.
cards.body:
Stuart's downtown public dock will close July 6 for a $3 million renovation projected to be complete by next Fourth of July. The year-long project will nearly double the dock's capacity, expanding from 18 to 44 slips for both motorized and non-motorized vessels. The renovation will include a 7,500 square foot fixed dock, a 1,400 square foot floating dock and a smaller floating platform. The project is funded by a state grant and transportation impact fees. With more than 1,400 boaters using the dock annually, Stuart Mayor Sean Reed said the upgrades are designed to prevent storm damage during hurricanes and major storms.

During the closure, the city is accommodating businesses and boaters who rely on the dock for drop-off and pick-up. Tiki Taxi & Cruises, which operates off the dock, will be allowed to build a gate at the end of the downtown Stuart dock's non-floating section to continue boarding passengers. Austin Kuyrkendall, director of operations for Tiki Taxi & Cruises, said the dock plays a central role in the city's identity and economy. He acknowledged the dock's current limitations, particularly on busy weekends when finding spots can be difficult, and said modernizing and expanding the dock will benefit both the city and businesses that depend on it.

cards.headline: Delray Beach area golf training center delayed 3 months, costs owner $90,000 after contractor problems
cards.teaser: Tom Molen, owner of Tee Box, a new virtual golf training and performance center near Delray Beach along Jog Road south of Linton Boulevard, said the project was delayed by three months after problems with the contractor hired to prepare the space.
cards.body:
Tom Molen, owner of Tee Box, a virtual golf training and performance center preparing to open near Delray Beach along Jog Road south of Linton Boulevard, faced a three-month delay and approximately $90,000 in costs due to contractor problems. The project was scheduled to open in April but was postponed after the hired contractor repeatedly delayed work. Although the contractor was licensed, Molen said the work ultimately had to be redone, creating additional expenses. The $90,000 estimate does not include revenue lost during delays or the cost of bringing in another contractor to fix the problems. "It was double pay on a lot of things from electricians to HVAC to drywall," Molen said.

David Allan, founder of Code Pro of the Palm Beaches, said contractor-related issues are impacting a significant number of people across Palm Beach County. He estimates 25% to 35% of homeowners and property owners face major issues with unvetted contractors. Allan recommends using Palm Beach County's online portal to verify whether contractors have proper licenses and insurance before work begins. According to Allan, the most common contractor complaints in Palm Beach County involve roofing, windows, and air conditioning work. Despite the setbacks, Molen said he is moving forward with Tee Box's grand opening scheduled for July 17.

cards.headline: Hobe Sound community raises funds for man who lost fiancee in deadly home fire
cards.teaser: Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside the couple's home in Hobe Sound. Preliminary findings from the sheriff's office point to an electrical issue as a possible cause.
cards.body:
A Hobe Sound man is rebuilding after losing his fiancée in a deadly home fire. Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside the couple's home. Preliminary findings from the sheriff's office point to an electrical issue as a possible cause. The fire remains under investigation. Friends have since launched a fundraiser to help Mark rebuild after the flames destroyed many of his and White's belongings.

Nina Fenn, a friend of White's for eight years, spoke about the loss. Fenn said White was a Christian woman who loved gardening, plants, and playing the piano. "She was always the first to lend a hand," Fenn said. "She loves kids; she loves her kids. She loves people." The loss is compounded by grief Mark has already endured. Mark lost his one and only child, Jacob, tragically. White's death adds another layer of heartbreak because her birthday is the Fourth of July. She passed just a few days before her birthday. "She's always been a good soul to me. She'll always be in our hearts," Fenn said.

cards.headline: Fourth of July cookout costs rise 4% this year, ground beef and strawberries see biggest jumps
cards.teaser: According to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey, a holiday meal for 10 now costs $73.82, up 4% from a year ago.
cards.body:
The Fourth of July cookout tradition is becoming more expensive this year. According to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey, a holiday meal for 10 now costs $73.82, up 4% from a year ago. Inflation is the primary culprit behind the price increases. Ground beef prices have risen 5.5%, while buns are up 7.7%. Strawberries, impacted by a Florida frost, have seen the largest increase at 12.4%. Ice cream prices have also climbed 5.3%.

Some items, however, offer relief to shoppers. Potato prices are down this year, benefiting those planning potato chips and salads. Corn prices have fluctuated, though locally grown corn from the Glades can provide the best value. Budgeting expert Andrea Woroch recommends shopping strategically by comparing stores for the best deals on groceries. She emphasized that cutting down food waste is crucial for families, and this process begins with creating a meal plan. Local shoppers are adapting their menus accordingly, with some planning hamburgers, coleslaw, chips, beer, burnt ends, mashed potatoes, and fresh broccoli, while others noted their living situations, such as condo restrictions, affect their grilling plans.

cards.headline: Breast cancer patient's insurance denies reconstruction surgery hours before scheduled procedure
cards.teaser: Beth Clark, 48, was denied coverage for a reconstruction procedure less than 24 hours before it was scheduled after her insurance company, Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield, called the surgery investigational.
cards.body:
Three months ago, Beth Clark, 48, was diagnosed with invasive ductal carcinoma, the most common type of breast cancer. She decided on a full double bilateral mastectomy with reconstruction. Clark had the mastectomy, but less than 24 hours before her reconstruction surgery, her insurance company, Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield, denied coverage for the procedure. According to her denial letter, the surgery involved a surgical mesh called GalaFlex, which the insurer considered "investigational" with "no or not enough proof it improves health." GalaFlex is a synthetic surgical mesh approved by the FDA for some uses in the body, but not for breast reconstruction. In a 2023 letter to health care providers, the FDA stated its "efficacy and safety for breast cancer patients have not been determined."

Dr. Alicia Billington, Clark's plastic surgeon, uses GalaFlex mesh on most of her breast reconstruction patients and believes insurance companies should reconsider their coverage policies. Billington has joined doctors taking their frustrations to social media and calling out insurers by name. Last year, after investigative reporting by Katie LaGrone and photojournalist Matthew Apthorp shared breast cancer patients' denial stories, Cigna became the first and only major insurer to start approving GalaFlex for breast reconstruction. Despite Anthem's denial, Clark received her reconstruction surgery with the GalaFlex mesh a little more than a week ago. Anthem stated the mesh "does not currently meet the standards required for coverage by our medical policy," but the company covers many other evidence-based alternatives. Clark and Billington are still fighting the denial.

hero.headline: Saint Andrew's Scots football eyes state title after 10-2 season and district championship
hero.body:
The Saint Andrew's Scots football team is working through the summer with a clear goal in mind: winning a state championship. After finishing the previous season with a 10-2 record and capturing the district title, the team felt they left opportunity on the table when they exited the playoffs in the second round. Now, with experienced leadership, they are determined to make a deeper postseason run.

Head coach Jimmy Robertson credits the team's veteran makeup as a major advantage heading into the 2026 fall season. The majority of the senior class has been with the program since middle school, giving them a deep understanding of the program's culture and standards. Robertson believes this continuity gives the Scots their best chance to achieve their goals. "Most of these seniors are four-year seniors, if not the majority of them came from the middle school as well. So they know how things are run. They had a lot of success in their career, and hopefully their senior year is the best season that we've had," Robertson said.

To prepare for a stronger playoff push, Saint Andrew's has intentionally scheduled more difficult opponents for the upcoming season. Senior Jack Williams explained the rationale behind this decision, saying the team wants to test itself against quality competition to elevate its level of play and attract attention to the program. Senior Jack Whelche emphasized that regular season success, while important, is secondary to playoff advancement. "A better year is just gonna be going farther in the playoffs. Obviously we wanna go undefeated in the season, but that doesn't matter if we keep losing in the second round of the playoffs," Whelche said.

The team is using summer workouts as a foundation for their ambitions. Senior Edmyer St. Jean highlighted how daily training sessions provide motivation and accountability as the players prepare for what they hope will be a historic season. The Scots are focused on breaking their previous records while leveraging their experienced senior class to make a state title run. With their experienced roster, challenging schedule, and clear objectives, Saint Andrew's believes they have what it takes to advance further in the postseason and compete for a state championship this fall.

cards.headline: Martin County maritime teams deploy two boats with medics for Fourth of July weekend
cards.teaser: Martin County Maritime Response Unit has two boats with medics on standby in the north and south as hundreds of boaters take to the water for the holiday weekend.
cards.body:
Lt. Brett Harry with Martin County Maritime Response Unit said the team is expecting hundreds of boaters on the water celebrating the Fourth of July weekend. The unit has deployed two boats with medics on standby in Martin County in the north and south to assist anyone in need.

Harry said the team is out on the water to help with anything from something as simple as a stubbed toe to cardiac issues, potential spinal injuries or other emergencies. Boaters like Brendan and Ashley Shannon launched from the ramps at Sandsprit Park in Martin County on Friday with their young daughter and puppy. The Shannons said safety is top of mind when hitting the water. Harry encouraged boaters to do their part by keeping their eyes on the water, having a designated driver, and packing life vests, whistles and flotation devices. "Just have fun and be safe," Harry said.

cards.headline: Hobe Sound community raises funds for man who lost fiance Misty Dawn White in deadly home fire
cards.teaser: Nina Fenn and other friends have launched a fundraiser to help Mark rebuild after a fire destroyed his home and killed his fiance Misty Dawn White just days before her birthday.
cards.body:
Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside her home in Hobe Sound she shared with her fiancé Mark. Preliminary findings from the sheriff's office point to an electrical issue as a possible cause. The fire remains under investigation.

Nina Fenn, a friend of White's for eight years, learned of the death through a phone call from Mark. Friends have since launched a fundraiser to help Mark rebuild after the flames destroyed many of his and White's belongings. Fenn described the scene as "completely a state of devastation." White was a Christian woman who loved gardening, plants and playing the piano. Fenn said White was always the first to lend a hand, loved kids and loved people. The loss is compounded by tragedy Mark has already endured. Mark lost his one and only child, Jacob. Adding to the heartbreak, Misty's birthday is the Fourth of July, and she passed away just days before her birthday. Fenn said White's memory will live on in the hearts of those who loved her.

cards.headline: Stuart downtown dock closing July 6 for $3 million renovation to nearly double slip capacity
cards.teaser: The dock will close for a year-long renovation that will expand capacity from 18 to 44 slips for motorized and non-motorized vessels, with completion projected for next Fourth of July.
cards.body:
Stuart's downtown public dock will close July 6 for a $3 million renovation projected to be complete by next Fourth of July. The project will nearly double the dock's capacity, expanding from 18 to 44 slips for both motorized and non-motorized vessels. The renovation will include a 7,500 square foot fixed dock, a 1,400 square foot floating dock and a smaller floating platform. The project is funded by a state grant and transportation impact fees.

Stuart Mayor Sean Reed said the upgrades are designed to prevent storm damage during hurricanes and major storms. With more than 1,400 boaters using the dock annually, the city is working to accommodate businesses during the closure. Tiki Taxi & Cruises, which operates off the dock, will continue running during construction. Austin Kuyrkendall, director of operations for Tiki Taxi & Cruises, said the city is allowing the business to build a gate at the end of the downtown Stuart dock on the non-floating section for boarding. Boat captain Parker Fisher said the dock has needed work over the years and he is glad the city is putting money into it.

cards.headline: Martin County School Board fights judge's order to reinstate Spectrum Academy teacher Matt Theobald
cards.teaser: The school board filed a court challenge arguing that removing Matt Theobald for Facebook comments about Charlie Kirk was appropriate and that an administrative law judge erred in recommending reinstatement.
cards.body:
The Martin County School Board is pushing back against a judge's recommendation to reinstate Matt Theobald, a social studies teacher at Spectrum Academy since 2009 who was suspended following controversial social media comments about Charlie Kirk. Theobald's Facebook post labeled Kirk as racist, misogynistic and a neo-Nazi. In a Thursday court filing, the school board argued Administrative Law Judge Jodi-Ann Vanessa Livingstone erred in recommending Theobald get his job back, claiming "numerous findings ... are not based upon competent substantial evidence." The board's attorney says Theobald's Facebook post about Kirk was a "serious offense" and removing him was appropriate.

In an order issued last month, Livingstone cited a recent Florida Fifth District Court of Appeal ruling that said disciplining a teacher for personal Facebook posts made off school grounds, on personal equipment, with no student involvement, violated the teacher's First Amendment rights. The judge also recommended Theobald be awarded back pay and benefits. According to an investigation report, Theobald admitted writing the comments about Kirk but said they were posted on his mother's private Facebook page "within a discussion among personal acquaintances" and were not intended for public view. The school board has the final say on whether Theobald gets his job back, with no clear timeline for a final decision.

cards.headline: Lantana veteran Stephen McCoy gets lien removed and roof fixed after WPTV investigation
cards.teaser: Stephen McCoy said Seabreeze Roofing and Sheet Metal in Boynton Beach left two holes unfinished on his home and stopped responding after he paid more than $17,000.
cards.body:
Stephen McCoy, a disabled and retired veteran in Lantana, sought help from WPTV after months of frustration with Seabreeze Roofing and Sheet Metal in Boynton Beach. McCoy hired the company to replace his nearly 20-year-old roof before hurricane season and made six payments totaling more than $17,000. While mostly satisfied with the work, McCoy said the company left two holes unfinished on the back side of his home. After the company stopped responding to his calls, texts and emails between January 10 and February, letters arrived from Gulfeagle Supply warning that a nearly $7,000 lien had been filed on his home. The lien document indicated Gulfeagle Supply had furnished materials to Seabreeze Roofing for McCoy's property but was not paid for those supplies.

When WPTV investigative reporter Kate Hussey visited Seabreeze Roofing, the owner declined to comment on camera citing legal reasons. Within an hour, Hussey returned to McCoy's home with a final waiver of lien signed by Gulfeagle Supply and notarized, lifting the lien. McCoy also learned the contractor would send crews back to finish the two problem areas on his roof. About an hour after receiving the waiver, McCoy sent WPTV a photo showing crews back on his roof completing the work.

cards.headline: Breast cancer patient Beth Clark denied coverage for reconstruction surgery hours before procedure
cards.teaser: Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield denied coverage for Beth Clark's reconstruction surgery involving GalaFlex mesh less than 24 hours before it was scheduled, citing the treatment as investigational.
cards.body:
Beth Clark, 48, was diagnosed with invasive ductal carcinoma three months ago and underwent a full double bilateral mastectomy with planned reconstruction. Less than 24 hours before her reconstruction surgery, her insurance company Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield denied coverage for the procedure. According to her denial letter, the surgery involving a surgical mesh called GalaFlex is still considered "investigational" and "there is no or not enough proof it improves health."

GalaFlex is a synthetic surgical mesh that has become a controversial treatment for breast reconstruction. While it is popular among plastic surgeons and approved by the FDA for some uses in the body, it is not approved for breast reconstruction and is still considered an off-label, investigational and experimental treatment. In a 2023 letter to health care providers, the FDA reiterated that its efficacy and safety for breast cancer patients have not been determined. Despite the insurer's denial, Clark got her reconstruction surgery with the GalaFlex mesh a little more than a week ago thanks to Dr. Alicia Billington, her plastic surgeon, finding a mechanism to make it happen. Clark and Billington are still fighting the denial.

hero.headline: Loggerhead Marinelife Center in Juno Beach offers sea turtle nesting programs through September
hero.body:
Loggerhead Marinelife Center in Juno Beach is offering educational and interactive programs during peak sea turtle nesting season through September. Guests can participate in guided Turtle Walks, the Hatchling Discovery Program, Hatchling Releases, Tidal Tots and Plastic Free July Community Action Day. According to the center, the programs are designed to give visitors an opportunity to learn more about sea turtle conservation along one of the world's busiest sea turtle nesting beaches.

The Turtle Walk program allows participants to observe the nesting process while learning about sea turtle biology, conservation and ongoing research efforts. Educational demonstrations may include the use of red-light headlamps, amber lighting, night scopes and research tag scanning equipment. The center's education and research departments work together during nesting season to collect and analyze data related to nesting activity and hatchling success. Sea turtle nesting season in Florida typically runs from March through October. Registration information and program details are available through Loggerhead Marinelife Center.

cards.headline: North Palm Beach hosts Fourth of July celebration with fireworks and America 250 events
cards.teaser: North Palm Beach residents and visitors will celebrate Independence Day with a full day of family-friendly activities, live entertainment and fireworks at North Palm Beach Country Club and The Clubhouse on July 4.
cards.body:
The free community event includes a pool party, lawn games, live music, a barbecue buffet and a fireworks finale scheduled for 9 p.m. Organizers say this years event also recognizes Americas 250th anniversary, bringing an added sense of celebration to the annual holiday tradition in Palm Beach County.

The festivities begin with a community pool party from 11 a.m. at the country club pool area. Guests can enjoy a water slide, DJ entertainment, games and activities, food and beverages and a poolside satellite bar. Beginning at 4:30 p.m., families can take part in activities including cornhole, Connect 4, giant Jenga, face painting and lawn games. Live music from Solstice Reign is expected to begin around 6 p.m.

Ashley Shipman, director of parks and recreation, said the golf course will offer one of the best locations to watch the fireworks display. The Clubhouse will also host a Fourth of July barbecue buffet from 4:30 p.m.

hero.headline: Secretary of State Byrd Moves to Block Paula Stark from Ballot After Incomplete Filing
hero.body:
Secretary of State Cord Byrd is asking courts to keep St. Cloud Republican Paula Stark off the ballot after she failed to submit required paperwork before the June 12 qualifying deadline. Stark submitted her materials just 30 minutes before the noon deadline, but state employees say she never filed Form 6, a public disclosure of financial interests. Stark has since sued to get on the ballot, claiming her treasurer Joel Davis accidentally received the form back during the submission process.

In response to her lawsuit, Byrd cast doubt on Stark's account of events. Five state employees submitted sworn declarations stating that Davis never submitted Form 6 and was not accidentally handed it back when he turned in other paperwork. Election Records Division Bureau Chief Erica Ikay Reeve noted in court filings that Stark still has not submitted Form 6 three weeks after the qualifying deadline. "Without seeing the Form 6 that was allegedly submitted, we cannot review it for facial sufficiency in order to determine if Candidate Stark would have qualified," Reeve stated. Byrd argued that Stark and Davis should have exercised greater care by questioning why the form was allegedly returned or by submitting documents earlier rather than waiting until the final moments before the deadline.

Reeve documented a troubling pattern of paperwork violations in Stark's campaign history. Davis has filed campaign finance reports more than a month late, reported excessive contributions, and maintained an incorrect address on file. Audits in the 2022 and 2024 election cycles found inconsistent amounts transferred between accounts and accounting discrepancies. The state revoked Stark's Friends of Paula political committee in November over 16,000 dollars in unpaid fines from missed campaign finance deadlines. In the 2024 cycle, a failure to pay a late report fine upheld by the Florida Elections Commission was referred to debt collection in November 2025. Of the 12 candidates who failed to properly submit Form 6, half of them corrected the problems and still qualified.

Byrd emphasized the time constraints in his court response, noting that ballots must be mailed to overseas military and their families by July 4, with vote-by-mail ballots due July 9 through 16. If Stark remains off the ballot, the August primary for House District 47 in Osceola and Orange counties becomes open to all voters choosing between Democrats Jorge Figueroa and Anthony Nieves. No other Republicans filed to run in the traditionally Democratic district, making Stark's exclusion a significant win for Florida Democrats.

cards.headline: St. Petersburg Selects $8.1 Billion Plan to Redevelop Tropicana Field Site
cards.teaser: Mayor Ken Welch selected a proposal to transform 58 acres around Tropicana Field into a mixed-use district centered on a 13-acre civic park and permanent home for The Woodson African American Museum of Florida.
cards.body:
St. Petersburg selected The Burg Bid, an $8.1 billion proposal led by Blake Investment Partners and Related Group, to redevelop Tropicana Field and the surrounding Historic Gas Plant District. The plan calls for purchasing 58 acres of city-owned land for $275 million, with a $20 million deposit due when a purchase and sale agreement is executed. The team values the full land package at $405 million when factoring in $130 million in land the city would retain. The proposal centers on Samuel Davis Park, a 13-acre civic and cultural space that would anchor 18.5 acres of total public park space. The park would house The Woodson African American Museum of Florida, a planned Museum of Public Art, a Discovery Center, event lawns, a playground, a splash pad, cafe areas, public art and a concert lawn.

The Burg Bid calls for 3,600 income-restricted housing units over a 15-year buildout, with 1,800 units planned within the Historic Gas Plant District and another 1,800 on complementary sites elsewhere in St. Petersburg. The plan includes homeownership opportunities at a discount to market value. Development would occur in three phases of approximately five years each, with early work potentially beginning outside the Tropicana Field footprint before stadium demolition. The proposal also includes a surf wave attraction, recreation deck, multimodal hub, workforce and small-business center called the Collaboratorium, and Resilience Event Center. The Rays lease with the city ends after the 2028 season.

cards.headline: DeSantis Allies Accuse Lieutenant Governor's Wife of Running Anonymous Attack Accounts
cards.teaser: Multiple social media accounts critical of Governor Ron DeSantis were suddenly deactivated after prominent communications veterans tied them to Layla Collins, wife of Lieutenant Governor Jay Collins.
cards.body:
Christina Pushaw, a communications specialist in the Governor's Office, and Jeremy Redfern, Deputy Chief of Staff to Attorney General James Uthmeier, accused Layla Collins of operating anonymous social media accounts attacking Governor Ron DeSantis. Pushaw shared information from Promota CEO Robert Salvador showing that the account @FSUdude01670 appeared connected to a phone number similar to one known to be associated with Layla Collins. Florida Politics obtained screenshots verifying the connection through two-factor authentication, which displayed an attempt to access the account that triggered a message to an email address with letters starred out and a phone number showing only the last digits. Pushaw also identified a second account, @bobnamy1, that appeared tied to Layla Collins. She noted the account content consisted entirely of two types of posts: promoting Jay Collins and attacking people who did not endorse him, including the governor. Redfern stated that the FSUDude account was tied directly to her personal cell phone number.

Both accounts were deactivated after Pushaw and Redfern publicly leveled their criticisms. Both previously served as Press Secretaries for DeSantis. Redfern now works for Uthmeier, who has endorsed U.S. Representative Byron Donalds for Governor. DeSantis appointed Jay Collins as Lieutenant Governor last year but has declined to endorse a preferred successor in the Governor's race. DeSantis cannot seek a third term because of term limits. Florida Politics requested comments from Jay and Layla Collins.

hero.headline: Hobe Sound woman dies in home fire days before her birthday, community raises funds for fiance
hero.teaser: Misty Dawn White, 46, died Monday after a fire broke out inside her Hobe Sound home. Friends are raising money to help her fiance Mark rebuild after the flames destroyed their belongings.
hero.body:
Misty Dawn White, 46, died in a house fire Monday in Hobe Sound. Investigators from the sheriff's office are still examining the blaze, though preliminary findings suggest an electrical issue may have caused it. Her fiancé Mark was not in the home at the time of the fire.

Nina Fenn, who had been White's friend for eight years, learned of the tragedy through a phone call from Mark. Fenn returned to the scene in the days after the fire to grieve and process what happened. "It's just a terrible shame and awful loss of life," Fenn said. The community has rallied around Mark by launching a fundraiser to help him rebuild. The flames destroyed many of his and White's belongings, leaving them facing significant loss.

White's death carries added heartbreak for those closest to her. Her birthday was just days away on the Fourth of July, making the timing particularly painful for her loved ones. The loss is especially difficult for Mark, who has already endured profound grief in his life. According to Fenn, Mark previously lost his only child, Jacob, in what she described as a tragic event. "Mark lost his one and only child, Jacob, and lost him tragically. So, I just am trying whatever I can to support him," Fenn said.

Fenn remembered White as someone who made a positive impact on everyone around her. White was a Christian woman who had many passions and talents. "Misty was a Christian woman. She loved gardening and plants. She plays the piano," Fenn said. "She was always the first to lend a hand. She loves kids; she loves her kids. She loves people." Those who knew her describe a woman with a generous spirit who was always ready to help others. As Fenn reflected on their friendship, she expressed her hope that White's memory would endure. "She's always been a good soul to me. She'll always be in our hearts," Fenn said. The community's response through the fundraiser demonstrates how deeply White touched the lives of those around her and the support they continue to show Mark during this difficult time.

cards.headline: Martin County Maritime Response Unit deploys medics as Fourth of July weekend brings hundreds of boaters
cards.teaser: Martin County Maritime Response Unit is deploying two boats with medics on standby this Fourth of July weekend as hundreds of boaters are expected on local wate.

Boaters launched Friday from Sandsprit Park in Martin County, including Brendan and Ashley Shannon, who arrived with their young daughter and puppy. "Just have fun and be safe," Harry said.

cards.teaser: The Martin County School Board filed a court document Thursday arguing against a judge's recommendation to reinstate Matt Theobald, a social studies teacher suspended for Facebook comments about Charlie Kirk.

The Martin County School Board filed a court challenge Thursday to a judge's recommendation to reinstate Matt Theobald, a social studies teacher at Spectrum Academy since 2009. In the filing, the school board's attorney argued that Administrative Law Judge Jodi-Ann Vanessa Livingstone's findings "are not based upon competent substantial evidence" and contended that Theobald's Facebook post about Kirk constituted "a serious offense" warranting his removal.

Judge Livingstone cited a recent Florida Fifth District Court of Appeal ruling in her recommendation, noting that disciplining a teacher for personal Facebook posts made off school grounds on personal equipment with no student involvement violated First Amendment rights. She also recommended Theobald receive back pay and benefits. According to an investigation report, Theobald admitted writing the comments but said they were posted on his mother's private Facebook page "within a discussion among personal acquaintances" and were not intended for public view. The school board retains final authority to decide whether Theobald returns to his position, with no timeline announced for that determination.

cards.headline: Fire crews extinguish abandoned structure fire in Jensen Beach
cards.teaser: Multiple agencies responded to extinguish a fire at an abandoned structure in Jensen Beach early Saturday morning.
cards.body:
Fire crews from multiple agencies responded to an abandoned structure fire in Jensen Beach early Saturday morning. The fire was extinguished by responding agencies.

cards.headline: Salty Pelican Fish Shack in Hobe Sound featured in Florida restaurant review
cards.teaser: The Salty Pelican Fish Shack, a restaurant in Hobe Sound, was the subject of a recent Florida restaurant review.
cards.body:
The Salty Pelican Fish Shack in Hobe Sound has been featured in a Florida restaurant review. The establishment is located in Hobe Sound.

The restaurant was highlighted in a review published Saturday. The Salty Pelican Fish Shack serves seafood to customers in the Hobe Sound area.

cards.headline: Four restaurants in Stuart and Jensen Beach highlighted in Florida dining feature
cards.teaser: A roundup of favorite Florida restaurants spotlighted four dining establishments in Stuart and Jensen Beach.
cards.body:
Four restaurants located in Stuart and Jensen Beach were featured in a Florida dining roundup published Friday. The feature highlighted favorite restaurants in the two Martin County communities.

The restaurants are located in Stuart and Jensen Beach, two towns on the Treasure Coast. The dining feature was published Friday evening.

cards.headline: Sandsprit Park hosts boaters launching for Fourth of July weekend
cards.teaser: Boaters including the Shannon family launched from Sandsprit Park in Martin County on Friday to celebrate the Fourth of July weekend on the water.
cards.body:
Brendan and Ashley Shannon launched from the ramps at Sandsprit Park in Martin County on Friday with their young daughter and puppy, joining hundreds of boaters hitting the waterways across Florida to celebrate the Fourth of July weekend. The Shannons said safety is top of mind when hitting the water.

His team will have two boats with medics on standby in Martin County in the north and south. "We're just out there to mitigate anybody that needs help, whether it's something as simple as a stubbed toe to anything cardiac related, or potential spinal injuries, or anything like that," Harry said. Harry recommended boaters keep their eyes on the water, have a designated driver, and pack life vests, whistles and flotation devices. "Just have fun and be safe," Harry said.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie advances $95 million Midway Road widening and new Florida Turnpike interchange
hero.body:
Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance last month to transfer 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation for a partial interchange at the Florida Turnpike. The city will vote on final approval at an upcoming meeting. According to Scott Samples, strategic communications manager for Port St. Lucie, the interchange addresses a significant gap in Turnpike access points. "This is a way for us to try to accommodate the growth that's already occurred, but also the growth that will occur over the next 20 to 50 years," Samples said.

FDOT has been constructing the $95 million Midway Road Widening Project to address congestion and safety concerns. The first phase widens the road from two lanes to four lanes between Selvitz Road and Jenkins Road. The second phase, from Jenkins Road to Glades Cut Off Road, remains in the design phase with construction anticipated to begin in Summer 2027. FDOT is also improving the Turnpike bridge and designing the partial interchange, which is still in development. The project will add bike and pedestrian paths along with sidewalks. Resident Erin Scheumeister acknowledged the construction is disruptive but necessary. "We definitely needed it to be expanded. It'll be a lot better and easier to get to work," she said.

cards.headline: Costco plans first Treasure Coast store in Port St. Lucie
cards.teaser: Costco is planning its first location on the Treasure Coast in Port St. Lucie.
cards.body:
The wholesale retailer is moving forward with plans to open a store in Port St. Lucie, marking the first Costco location on the Treasure Coast. The development represents a major retail addition to St. Lucie County.

The store would bring a new shopping option to Port St. Lucie residents who currently must travel outside the area to access Costco locations.

cards.headline: Body of missing diver recovered near Fort Pierce Inlet
cards.teaser: Deputies recovered the body of a missing diver on the Florida coast near Fort Pierce Inlet.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office reported finding the body of a diver who had been reported missing near Fort Pierce Inlet. The recovery took place on the Florida coast in the Fort Pierce area.

Authorities had been searching for the missing diver before the body was located.

cards.headline: Two people rescued after boat sinks in Intracoastal Waterway in St. Lucie County
cards.teaser: Rescuers pulled two people from the water after their boat sank in the Intracoastal Waterway in St. Lucie County.
cards.body:
Two boaters were rescued from the Intracoastal Waterway in St. Lucie County after their vessel sank. Emergency responders pulled both people from the water safely.

Bodycam footage captured the rescue operation as crews worked to save the boaters from the sinking vessel.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce man arrested on child pornography charges
cards.teaser: The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office arrested a Fort Pierce man on child pornography charges.
cards.body:
A Fort Pierce resident was taken into custody by the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office on charges related to child pornography. The sheriff's office announced the arrest following an investigation.

The case remains under investigation by local authorities.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce woman recognized for supporting little free libraries
cards.teaser: A Fort Pierce woman received recognition for her work supporting little free libraries in the community.
cards.body:
A Fort Pierce resident was honored for her contributions to supporting little free libraries throughout the area. The recognition highlights her efforts to promote literacy and community access to books.

Little free libraries provide neighborhood book sharing stations where residents can take or leave books for others to read.

cards.headline: Legacy Lions football team standings updated for Port St. Lucie high school
cards.teaser: The Legacy Lions football team standings have been updated for the Port St. Lucie high school program.
cards.body:
Current football standings for the Legacy Lions in Port St. Lucie show the team's position for the season. The standings track the high school football program's performance.

Legacy high school competes in Port St. Lucie area football programs.

hero.headline: Fourth of July cookout costs up 4 percent across Florida
hero.teaser: Holiday meals for Independence Day celebrations cost more this year, with a cookout for 10 people now running $73.82 according to national survey data.
hero.body:
The American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey shows that a Fourth of July meal for 10 people now costs $73.82, up 4 percent from last year. Inflation is driving the price increases across key cookout items. Ground beef prices rose 5.5 percent, while buns increased 7.7 percent. Strawberries experienced the steepest jump at 12.4 percent after a Florida frost damaged crops. Ice cream prices climbed 5.3 percent. Potato prices declined this year, offering relief for shoppers buying potato chips and salad ingredients. Corn prices have fluctuated, but locally grown corn from the Glades can offer better deals.

Budgeting expert Andrea Woroch recommended comparison shopping between stores and cutting down food waste through meal planning. Shoppers interviewed Friday described their holiday meal plans, which included hamburgers, steak, coleslaw, chips, burnt ends, mashed potatoes, baked potatoes and fresh broccoli. Some noted challenges like preparing meals in limited spaces, such as condos without grills.

cards.headline: Vero Beach buries time capsule to be opened in 2076
cards.teaser: A community-wide time capsule was buried in Vero Beach on Friday, with plans to open it 50 years from now in 2076.
cards.body:
Vero Beach conducted a ceremony to bury a community-wide time capsule that will remain sealed until 2076. The capsule was interred on Friday as part of a community project involving local residents.

The time capsule is scheduled to be opened in 50 years, providing future residents a glimpse into life in Vero Beach in 2026. Community members participated in the project, which preserves artifacts and materials from the current era.

The burial took place in Vero Beach, though specific details about the contents of the capsule and its exact location were part of the community event held Friday.

cards.headline: Indian River State College Promise Program offers debt-free degrees to students
cards.body:
Indian River State College has implemented a Promise Program designed to help students graduate with college degrees without accumulating debt. The program provides financial support to eligible students attending the college, which serves multiple counties across the Treasure Coast region.

The Promise Program aims to remove financial barriers that prevent students from completing their education. Indian River State College operates campuses in multiple locations across the region, offering associate degrees and other credentials to students in the area.

The program helps students achieve what administrators describe as the dream of earning a debt-free college degree. By covering costs that traditional financial aid may not address, the initiative seeks to increase college completion rates among local students.

Details about the specific eligibility requirements and the scope of financial coverage provided by the Promise Program were announced by the college. Indian River State College continues to serve students across its service area with educational programs and support services.

cards.headline: Fireworks displays scheduled across Treasure Coast for Independence Day
cards.teaser: Multiple fireworks displays are planned across the Treasure Coast and Palm Beaches area for the Fourth of July weekend.
cards.body:
Communities across the Treasure Coast have scheduled fireworks displays for the Independence Day holiday. The displays are taking place throughout the Palm Beaches and Treasure Coast region as residents celebrate the Fourth of July.

The fireworks events are planned for Saturday, July 4, with multiple locations hosting celebrations. Residents across the area have access to public fireworks displays as part of the holiday weekend festivities.

cards.headline: Breast cancer patient denied coverage for reconstruction surgery hours before procedure
cards.teaser: Beth Clark, 48, received an insurance denial from Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield less than 24 hours before her scheduled breast reconstruction surgery.
cards.body:
Beth Clark, 48, was diagnosed with invasive ductal carcinoma three months ago and underwent a double bilateral mastectomy. Less than 24 hours before her scheduled reconstruction surgery, Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield denied coverage for the procedure involving GalaFlex surgical mesh. According to the denial letter, the insurance company considers the treatment "investigational" with "no or not enough proof it improves health." While GalaFlex is FDA-approved for some uses in the body, it is not approved for breast reconstruction and remains an off-label, experimental treatment. In a 2023 letter to health care providers, the FDA stated that the product's "efficacy and safety for breast cancer patients have not been determined."

Dr. Alicia Billington, Clark's plastic surgeon, uses GalaFlex mesh on most breast reconstruction patients and argues it is less risky than other options. Billington has joined other doctors in criticizing insurance denials on social media. Clark received her reconstruction surgery with the GalaFlex mesh about a week later after Billington found a way to make it happen. Anthem responded that without FDA approval, GalaFlex "does not currently meet the standards required for coverage by our medical policy," though the company covers other evidence-based alternatives and noted Clark has the right to appeal.

cards.headline: Riviera Beach named only Florida city to receive 2026 All-America City Award
cards.teaser: Riviera Beach was selected as one of 10 communities nationwide to receive the prestigious All-America City Award, making it the only Florida city honored this year.
cards.body:
Riviera Beach has been named one of 10 U.S. communities to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League, making it the only Florida city selected for this year's honor. The award was announced during the National Civic League conference in Denver and recognizes communities that bring residents, local government, businesses and organizations together to solve local challenges and create lasting change. Mayor Douglas Lawson called the recognition a proud moment for the city, saying Riviera Beach earned the award through long-term revitalization efforts. "They're seeing the changes; they're seeing the revitalization and the reimagining of Riviera Beach that we set out so many years to do," Lawson said.

The city's application highlighted several civic participation programs, including the Riviera Beach Youth Council for high school students, the Citizens Leadership Academy with a 98 percent completion rate, and the Neighborhood Reclaim Home Rehabilitation Program, which provides mini-grants to help longtime homeowners make critical repairs. Councilwoman KaShamba Miller-Anderson credited residents for the honor, saying the award belongs to the entire community. The All-America City Award has been presented annually since 1949 and is considered one of the nation's most respected civic honors. City leaders say the designation positions Riviera Beach for future opportunities and continued growth.

cards.headline: Saint Andrew's Scots football targets state title after 10-2 season
cards.teaser: The Saint Andrew's Scots finished last season 10-2 with a district championship but are setting sights higher after a second-round playoff exit.
cards.body:
The Saint Andrew's Scots football team finished last season with a 10-2 record and a district title, but a second-round playoff exit has the team hungry for more this fall. Head coach Jimmy Robertson said most of the seniors are four-year players who came through the middle school program, giving them deep familiarity with how the program operates. With a veteran senior class leading the way, the Scots are scheduling more challenging opponents for the 2026 season to compete at a higher level and attract new players.

Senior Jack Williams said the demanding schedule is designed to take the program to the next level by competing against quality teams. For the Scots, postseason success is the true measure of improvement. Senior Jack Whelche said advancing further in the playoffs matters more than regular season performance, noting that a second-round exit cannot happen again regardless of how many games the team wins. The team is using summer workouts as motivation, with senior Edmyer St. Jean saying the daily grind gives players something to work toward as they prepare to break records when the season begins.
